analysis.title: David vs. Goliath: RTY vs. NDX at Historical Extreme
key_insights: Since mid-August, Technology is +9.3% while eight other sectors are down 3% or worse and five are down 5% or worse.
The Russell 2000 (RTY) to Nasdaq 100 (NDX) ratio is down 16% since late July. Its 14-day RSI closed at 12.77, the 8th lowest day on record.

Since 1985 the RTY/NDX ratio's RSI has fallen below 14 in only three prior unique periods: July 2007, August 2011 and March 2020. BTIG calls a sample of three statistically insignificant and stresses the rarity of the reading.
The three first-close dates below 14 were 7/23/07, 8/5/11 and 3/18/20. In 2011 and 2020 the SPX had already been through extreme stress, while in 2007 the SPX was near its highs, as it is now.
In 2007 and 2011 the RTY/NDX ratio kept moving lower over the next 10 and 30 days, so an oversold reading does not mean the move is over.
In July 2007 the SPX broke out of a 6-week range to a new high, the breakout failed after a few days, and the SPX fell nearly 12% in the 'quant quake'.

Before the 2007 RTY/NDX oversold reading, 30-year yields rose about 75bps from mid-May to mid-June and CCC spreads widened about 150bps from early June to mid-July. The VIX closed at 15 on July 19, 2007.
Today 30-year yields are up 60bps in a month, CCC spreads are up 150bps in a month and 400bps in 6 months, and the VIX closed at 15, which BTIG says rhymes with 2007.

30-year yields show a 10-count on Bloomberg candle sessions, a sign of exhaustion, and faded about 4bps from intraday highs. BTIG still sees the primary trend for rates as higher but would not be surprised by a reversion lower over the next couple of weeks.

Falling rates should help RTY stabilize after its nearly 10% drawdown, but yields finished well off session highs while RTY barely finished off its lows. In 2007 falling yields coincided with falling RTY.
RTY is again testing its 200-day moving average. BTIG's conviction is higher that NDX 'catches down' than that RTY 'catches up'.

sector_views.rationale: Technology is +9.3% since mid-August while eight other sectors are down 3% or worse. BTIG expects NDX to 'catch down' to small caps rather than the reverse.
RTY/NDX is deeply oversold and rates may be exhausting, which could help RTY stabilize. History from 2007 and 2011 shows further relative declines, and RTY is testing its 200-day moving average.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A sharp bond sell-off resembles the 2007 setup that preceded equity weakness. A 10-count exhaustion signal suggests a possible pullback in yields over the next couple of weeks.
Widening junk spreads preceded the 2007 RTY/NDX oversold condition and equity weakness.
The VIX was also at 15 in July 2007, before the equity decline.

risk_factors: The SPX near its highs with weak breadth resembles July 2007, when a failed breakout led to a nearly 12% drop.
A bond sell-off combined with widening CCC spreads preceded equity weakness in 2007 and is present again now.
The RTY/NDX ratio kept falling over the next 10 and 30 days after the 2007 and 2011 oversold readings.
Falling yields may not help RTY, as they coincided with falling RTY in July and August 2007.
vol_and_positioning: The VIX closed at 15, the same level as on July 19, 2007.
RTY/NDX 14-day RSI of 12.77 is the 8th lowest reading since 1985.
30-year yields show a 10-count exhaustion signal on Bloomberg candle sessions and faded about 4bps from intraday highs.
